newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Chiwan Petroleum lower '96 net seen.
newsitem.headline: Chiwan Petroleum lower '96 net seen.

text.p: Shenzhen Chiwan Petroleum Supply Base Co Ltd is likely to post a drop in 1996 profit due to sluggish business, a company official said on Wednesday.
Oil drilling by foreign companies in the South China Sea declined last year which pulled down Chiwan's earnings, the official told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.
The company's results are still being audited and precise figures were not available, he said.

Chiwan Base, which provides support services for foreign firms exploring petroleum and natural gas reserves in the South China Sea, blamed a 18.8 percent drop in 1996 first-half net profit on its customers' delay in drilling new oil wells.

In its interim report last year, the company said it posted after-tax profit of US$3.24 million in the first half of 1996, down from US$3.99 million in the year-earlier period under Chinese accounting standards.
It did not give figures based on international standards.

The phasing out of its preferential tax status, which saw corporate income tax at a 15 percent in 1996 compared with 7.5 percent in the previous five years, also dragged down earnings, the company said.
The company's 1995 net profit rose 50.6 percent to US$8.172 million from US$5.426 million in 1994, due to expansion of its operations.
Chiwan Petroleum listed 60 million hard currency B shares on the Shenzhen stock exchange in mid-1995.
